messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Fri, Oct 18, 2024, Andriy Kovalenko via AMBER wrote:
>
>At present, I have installed Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS on my Dell Precision Tower
>5810 desktop from scratch, and have now been installing Amber24 and
>AmberTools24.
Hi Andriy:  sorry to be so slow in replying.  I'm hoping that someone with
access to Ubuntu 24.04 will be able to try to reproduce your problem.  I
have a request out for volunteers, but maybe someon reading this on the
Amber mailing list will be able to chime in.

messages.body:
Hello,
I've tried to reproduce the problem on an Ubuntu-24.04 container, but
couldn't. Amber was able to build without problem (except for the need to
install the OS boost package).
Checking your log, I wonder if you have some python problem. Several
python/conda environment installations? On your cmake log file, you have
the following line:
> -- Found PythonLibs:
> /home/andriy/amber24_src/build/CMakeFiles/miniconda/install/lib/
> libpython3.12.so (Required is exact version "3.11.9")
So 3.12 or 3.11.9?
On my side, I have the following line:
> -- Found PythonLibs:
> /app/amber24_src/build/CMakeFiles/miniconda/install/lib/libpython3.12.so
> (found suitable exact version "3.12.7")
This makes better sense.
You may have a 3.11.9 python installation somewhere in your PATH for which
cmake gets confused (imho).
In your install log, I see version conflicts here:
> byte-compiling
> /home/andriy/amber24//lib/python3.11/site-packages/ndfes/FES.py to
> FES.cpython-311.pyc
>
> /home/andriy/amber24//miniconda/lib/python3.12/site-packages/conda_build/convert.py
Best,
Gerald.
